headline: Panthers’ Matthew Tkachuk, Senators’ Nick Cousins fined following heated game
take:
Per The Athletic, Matthew Tkachuk was fined $5,000 for roughing after a scrum in Wednesday's Senators-Panthers game that also involved his brother Brady, who was seated on the Panthers bench. Daily Faceoff reports that Ottawa's Nick Cousins was fined as well after the third-period scuffle.

The fines are small, but the two players are far apart on the ice. So far this season, Tkachuk has 15 points in 10 games and plays 19.34 minutes a night. At five-on-five, FLA has had 60.66% of the expected goals (a measure of chance quality) while he is out there, and his team does about 10 percentage points better with him than without him. His 3 goals sit almost exactly on his own expected total of 2.84, so the scoring looks earned, not lucky.

Cousins is a fourth-line forward at 9.18 minutes a game, and the numbers are rough. OTT has just 24.13% of the five-on-five expected goals with him on the ice, and the team's share is about 32 points worse than when he sits. His 1 goal is well above his 0.43 expected, so even that small production has been generous. It's a small sample, but the picture is clear. One player drives play for a Florida team that has underperformed its chances, and the other is a minor piece for a 7-3-0 Ottawa team.
